done_when: After a retest, when the default branch moved again, merge checks the new commits against the item's changed files again and merges at once when none overlap; with an overlap it retests again; it stops only after five moves, and a test covers two moves in a row

known.title: P1: Recheck merge permission after accepting a new default branch

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Security
Case: normal use - the owner disables agent merges while combined tests or required checks are running in Forge's repo or a signed-off client.
Merge permission is checked only at entry (lines 45–47). This loop accepts a newly fetched default branch without checking that permission again. If the new commit sets `merge = "human"` and the item does not touch `forge.toml`, it is treated as disjoint and the pull request still merges. `repo.merge_setting` (src/forge/repo.py:683–686) derives permission from the default branch, but is never called again here. Recheck that existing permission before proceeding with the newly observed default.
Adds work: recheck merge permission after a default-branch move; F 1 x H 2 = 2; 2 x C = 2
findings.title: P1: Recheck merge permission after accepting a new default branch

why: On a busy day forge merge keeps stopping with 'The default branch moved again': after one retest it gives up when main moves during the retest, so items race each other and none merge (four in a row today, the sign-off hotfix among them)
